definition: A sliding window keeps a contiguous segment of a sequence and updates the answer as the segment moves, instead of recomputing it from scratch. Growing or shrinking the ends by one element updates a running aggregate. Many substring and subarray problems that look quadratic become linear this way.

complexity.time: Often O(n), when each index enters and leaves the window at most once.
complexity.space: Often O(1) or O(k) for the state inside the window.

examples: The maximum sum of any subarray of length k
The longest substring with no repeated character
